To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) NR metrics are able to correctly classify the quality of JPEG-distorted natural images; 2) a pool of NR metrics can reach better results than each single one; 3) the number of quality classes has an impact on the classification results; 4) the performance of the classifiers depends on the considered database.

(1) a pool of NR metrics outperforms the single ones, (2) the best results are obtained by considering three quality classes, and (3) the best results on all databases are obtained by using the three quality classes and the pool of metrics.
the best classification performance is obtained with a pool of metrics, and that the classification performance is higher for three classes rather than five.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) the use of a classification approach to IQA, (ii) a comparison among NR metrics and (iii) the use of the proposed approach to evaluate the quality of JPEG-compressed images.
a new approach for IQA, which is based on the classification of the quality scores given by NR metrics into different quality classes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single metric is not able to achieve the same performance as a pool of metrics.
the best performances are achieved by the classifiers based on a pool of NR metrics, and that the number of classes has a strong impact on the performances.
the best performance is reached by a pool of NR metrics, which outperform the best single metric.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classification approach is promising, and that a pool of metrics performs better than each of the considered single ones.
the classification of the images in quality classes is not possible with a high accuracy.
the proposed classification framework is a promising approach to IQA, which is able to outperform state-of-the-art NR metrics in terms of correlation with subjective scores.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the task of classifying images into quality classes, the best performance is achieved when the features are a pool of NR metrics, while the best performance is obtained with a 3-class classifier.
a pool of metrics is more effective than a single metric, and that a classifier trained on a database is more effective than one trained on the other databases.

the performance of the proposed classifiers is comparable to state of the art NR methods, but the proposed classifiers have the advantage of not being affected by the presence of noise, which is a typical issue for NR methods.
